about: The quality bar (docs/quality.md, story quality-ratchet): one entry per metric with its kind, direction, tolerance and source, and one bar per target. The bars are the first assessment's values; a value worse than its bar beyond the tolerance is refused, an improvement is written into the bar in the same change (IGNITE_BLESS=1), and a bar made worse than main's needs a decision. known_differences lists differences of the differential runner accepted until a story fixes them; eval_cannot_run lists the units the evaluator cannot run, with the reason; eval_slow names the decision that keeps a unit over the evaluator's time limit out of merge runs.
areas: Semantics: one meaning across the three consumers
Front end: the checker refuses exactly the wrong programs

llvm/terminald/dev.decision: Accepted for v0.16.0 (Timo, 2026-11-09): every todod and terminald binary grew 16 to 48 % over v0.15.0 (LLVM release todod 2,107,792 to 2,837,352 B, terminald 1,512,792 to 2,242,824 B; Rust target release todod 1,011,216 to 1,219,336 B). Measured by building at each merge of PR 131: the readiness scheduler (1a8aba78) is 96 % of the LLVM and 97 % of the Rust-target growth, U32 nothing, the leak census 3 to 4 %, wave 8 under 1 %. Which part of the scheduler takes the space is not measured; story readiness-binary-size cuts it.; accepted for v0.16.0 (Timo, 2026-11-10): the dev binaries on the LLVM target grew with TLS client sessions (story tls-client): terminald 9,144,568 to 15,560,616 B, todod 9,849,080 to 16,272,232 B; the release binaries are within their bars. The linker keeps the debug info of every runtime object it pulls in, and the TLS engine (rustls, ring, webpki) shares objects with code every program calls: the dev terminald holds 193 rustls, 163 ring and 51 webpki compile units. No debug info for the engine crates gave 10,732,272 B, that without ring's C and assembly debug info 9,760,088 B, both over the limit; story tls-engine-own-crates moves the engine into crates of its own and withdraws this decision
